description: Behavior evals — with the skill loaded, does React/TS output follow the component and testing conventions in references/?

evals.name: new-component-conventions
evals.prompt: Add a SearchBar component to this React + TypeScript app. It takes a placeholder and an onSearch callback, and calls onSearch with the input value when the user presses Enter.
evals.expected_output: A function component in SearchBar.tsx with a typed props interface, destructured props, no any, semantic input element with an accessible label, no class component, no speculative memoization.

assertions.text: Props defined as an explicit TypeScript interface
Input has an accessible identity (label, aria-label, or role)
No useMemo/useCallback/React.memo without a stated reason

evals.name: rtl-test-conventions
evals.prompt: Write tests for the existing LoginForm component: it should show a validation error when the email field is empty on submit, and call onSubmit with the credentials when both fields are filled.
evals.expected_output: A co-located LoginForm.test.tsx using React Testing Library with role/label queries, userEvent interactions, queryBy* for absence assertions, and behavior-stating test names.

assertions.text: Queries use getByRole/getByLabelText, not getByTestId as primary
No assertions on component internals (state, hook calls)

evals.name: no-useeffect-derived-state
evals.prompt: In this component, add a total price display that updates whenever the items array prop changes.
evals.expected_output: Total computed during render (plain derivation or useMemo only if measured/needed) — not mirrored into useState via useEffect.

assertions.text: Derived value computed during render, not stored in useState via useEffect
No new effect introduced for pure data transformation
